title: Fourier norm bounded by spectral sparsity
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $h$ be a sign-valued function on $\\{-1,1\\}^n$, and let $S$ be a nonnegative integer. Regard $h$ as a real-valued function via its sign values and as a function on the binary cube $\\mathbb F_2^n$ via the coordinatewise identification of binary values with signs. If at most $S$ of its binary Fourier coefficients are nonzero, then its Fourier one-norm on the sign cube is at most $S$.
hypotheses_covered: The binary Fourier support of the corresponding function on $\\mathbb F_2^n$ has cardinality at most $S$
